correctness.rationale: The pure-tensor zero-product span is an ideal; CRT kills off-diagonal blocks. The residue-field lift reduces each primary factor to a truncated polynomial local algebra, where valuation makes its diagonal zero-product ideal exactly the e-th power of the two-generated augmentation ideal. Galois tensor splitting then yields d copies of the fat-plane jet ring. The monomial basis gives D; multiplication has rank N and its dual subspace has codimension D-N. Exact exhaustive rank calculations passed all fourteen stated prime-field test cases, but the general proof rests on the algebraic lemmas, not on finite tests.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by the zero-Jordan-product-determination criterion, which only distinguishes whether the relevant bilinear-form defect vanishes. The theorem classifies the full natural quotient algebra and counts all bilinear zero-product preservers for every finite-field polynomial quotient; it identifies a concrete two-variable jet thickness and a Galois degree contribution, yielding a structural parameter family and a quantitative obstruction rather than a routine recomputation of the binary criterion.
